label: input h early in the original phase / e at t=0 / <DEL> in L=3 sequences
explanation: Fires on three disjoint input-driven components, all at the start of the sequence or the <DEL> step, and essentially never in the copy phase. (1) Input h at the first step (t=0): always active (precision 1.0), carrying about 43% of activation mass. h at t=2 or 3 also fires but less reliably (precision about 0.49 and 0.29, with no simple context found that separates the cases); h at t=1 or t>=4 almost never fires. (2) Input e at t=0: always active but weak (about 0.03 of max), about 26% of active steps but only about 4% of mass. (3) The <DEL> step of length-3 sequences: precision 0.79, about 29% of mass, and this is where the largest activations occur (top examples are all <DEL> at L=3, often after an h at t=2). <DEL> in longer sequences is only rarely and weakly active. Small leftovers: c/u/j at early positions, <DEL> at L=4.
